title: M-BRIDGE — the Windows bridge: the only thing that ever touches the desktop
desc:
DELIVERABLE: the Windows bridge in dreamer2664/mars — bridge/ + docs/BRIDGE.md (frozen v1, read it first) + tests. A tiny local service on the Director's Windows PC: it is the EXECUTOR. It holds no secrets; it reads world/lock.json and accepts an action ONLY when token+generation match the current grant (fencing, docs/WORLD.md section 4); it performs ONLY allowlisted actions; it returns a receipt per action (lock generation, timestamps, outcome, observable result) which the requesting agent records in the world. The bridge never writes the world state.
BROWSER ROAD (the Director's call): attach to a real browser over CDP — dedicated profile started once with --user-data-dir + --remote-debugging-port (Chrome 136+ ignores the port on the default profile); the Director logs into the channel accounts once in that profile. No API paperwork, no cookie export, no password ever in the project.
M1 ALLOWLIST: upload_file (path + target channel; verify the active channel chip in YouTube Studio before upload) · set_metadata (title/description/thumbnail) · read_published_url (confirm live, return url). Everything else refused by name.
PLUS: a dry-run mode and a Linux SIMULATOR (mock executor) so the crew tests the full protocol — acquire, act with correct gen, stale-gen refusal, wrong-token refusal, release — without Windows; fail-closed behavior (browser unreachable / unexpected dialog => act nothing, return ok:false, receipt says so; the lock is NOT released by the bridge — only the holder or expiry/sweep moves it); docs/BRIDGE.md's one-time setup section kept honest for a non-programmer.
EVIDENCE: simulator runs pasted (correct gen OK; stale gen refused with reason; wrong token refused); dry-run self-test output; the setup doc reviewed end-to-end as if by the Director.
OWNS: bridge/, docs/BRIDGE.md, tests/test_bridge_sim.py.
NOTE: the real end-to-end test happens on the Director's PC as the first M1 act, with him watching.
BRANCH: agent/<you>/<task-id>

Lifecycle vs real world.py: release kills the old grant, new holder gets a new generation, old token stays dead.
